source_text:
Tales etiam si occisi in confessione nominis fuerint, macula ista nec sanguine abluitur: inexpiabilis et grauis culpa discordiae nec passione purgatur. esse martyr non potest qui in ecclesia non eat: ad regnum peruenire non poterit qui eam quae regnatura est dereliquit. pacem nobis Christus dedit, concordes adque unanimes esse praecepit, dilectionis et caritatis foedera incorrupta adque inuiolata mandauit: exhibere se non potest martyrem qui fraternam non tenuit caritatem. docet hoc et contestatur Paulus apostolus dicens: et si habuero fidem ita ut montes transferam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil sum: et si in cibos distribuero omnia mea et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil proficio. caritas magnanima est, caritas benigna est, caritas non aemulatur, non inflatur, non inritatur, non agit perperam, non cogitat malum, omnia diligit, omnia credit, omnia sperat, omnia sustinet. caritas numquam excidet. numquam, inquit, excidet caritas. haec enim semper in regno erit, haec in aeternum fraternitatis sibi cohaerentis unitate durabit. ad regnum caelorum non potest peruenire discordia, ad praemium Christi qui dixit: hoc est mandatum meum ut diligatis
inuicem, quemadmodum dilexi uos, pertinere non poterit qui dilectionem Christi perfida dissensione uiolauit. qui caritatem non habet Deum non habet. Iohannis beati apostoli uoxest: Deus, inquit, dilectio est et qui manet in dilectione in Deo manet et Deus in illo manet. cum Deo manere non possunt qui esse in ecclesia Dei unanimes noluerunt. ardeant licet flammis et ignibus traditi uel obiecti bestiis animas suas ponant, non erit illa fidei corona sed poena perfidiae nec religiosae uirtutis exitus gloriosus sed desperationis interitus. occidi talis potest, coronari non potest. sic se christianum esse profitetur, quomodo et Christum diabolus saepe mentitur ipso Domino praemonente et dicente: multi uenient in nomine meo dicentes: ego sum Christus, e.t multos fallent. sicut ille Christus non est, quamuis fallat in nomine, ita nec christianus uideri potest qui non permanet in euangelio eius et fidei ueritate.
thought_title: No martyrdom or salvation outside the Church's unity and love
orientation: Cyprian is addressing those who have broken away from the Church, arguing that even suffering death for the name of Christ cannot cleanse the guilt of discord or make them martyrs.
pass_a_gloss: Such [ones] also if [they] have been killed in [the] confession of [the] name, [that] stain not even by blood is washed away: [the] inexpiable and heavy guilt of discord not even by passion is purged. [a] martyr cannot be [he] who in [the] church does not go: to [the] kingdom cannot arrive [he] who her which [is] about to reign has abandoned. peace to us Christ gave, [to be] concordant and unanimous he commanded, [the] covenants of affection and love incorrupt and inviolate he ordered: [he] cannot show himself [a] martyr who brotherly did not hold love. teaches this and testifies Paul [the] apostle saying: and if I shall have faith so that mountains I move, love however I do not have, nothing I am: and if in foods I shall distribute all my [things] and if I shall hand over my body so that it burns, love however I do not have, nothing I profit. love magnanimous is, love kind is, love not is envious, not is puffed up, not is provoked, not acts wrongly, not thinks evil, all [things] loves, all [things] believes, all [things] hopes, all [things] endures. love never will fail. never, he says, will fail love. this [one] for always in [the] kingdom will be, this [one] in eternity of brotherhood to itself clinging by unity will endure. to [the] kingdom of heavens cannot arrive discord, to [the] reward of Christ who said: this is my commandment that you love one another, just as I have loved you, cannot belong [he] who [the] love of Christ by faithless dissension has violated. [he] who love does not have God does not have. of John [the] blessed apostle [the] voice is: God, he says, love is and [he] who remains in love in God remains and God in him remains. with God to remain cannot [those] who in [the] church of God [to be] unanimous have not wanted. let them burn even by flames and fires handed over or thrown to beasts [and] their souls lay down, not will be that [the] crown of faith but [the] punishment of faithlessness nor of religious virtue [the] glorious departure but of desperation [the] destruction. [to be] killed such [a one] can, [to be] crowned cannot. so himself [a] Christian to be he professes, just as also Christ [the] devil often lies [about] [the] Lord himself forewarning and saying: many will come in my name saying: I am Christ, and many they will deceive. just as that [one] Christ is not, although he deceives in [the] name, so neither [a] Christian can be seen [he] who does not remain in his gospel and [the] truth of faith.

lemmas.gloss: inexpiable, that cannot be atoned for

choices.english: this stain is not washed away even by blood
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of abluitur and the emphatic 'nec...sanguine' as 'not even by blood' to preserve the absolute negation.
rejected: this stain is not cleansed by blood
blood does not wash away this stain

choices.term: esse martyr non potest qui in ecclesia non eat
choices.english: He cannot be a martyr who is not in the Church
choices.why: The infinitive 'esse martyr' is kept as a predicate complement with 'cannot be,' and 'non eat' is rendered as present indicative 'is not' to match the source's simple present.
rejected: He who is not in the Church cannot be a martyr
No one outside the Church can be a martyr

choices.english: the covenants of affection and love
choices.why: Both 'dilectio' and 'caritas' are rendered distinctly as 'affection' and 'love' to preserve the double expression, and 'foedera' as 'covenants' to keep the legal/binding force.
rejected: the bonds of love and charity

choices.why: 'Excidet' is future tense, so 'will fall away' preserves the future; 'numquam' as 'never' keeps the absolute negation.
'Perfida' is rendered as 'faithless' to capture the betrayal of faith, and 'dissensione' as 'dissension' to keep the abstract noun of division.

choices.term: non erit illa fidei corona sed poena perfidiae
choices.english: that will not be the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness
choices.why: The contrast 'corona fidei' vs 'poena perfidiae' is kept as 'crown of faith' vs 'punishment of faithlessness' to preserve the wordplay on fides/perfidia.
rejected: that will not be the crown of faith but the penalty of treachery
that is not the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness

pass_b_english: Even if such people are killed while confessing the name, this stain is not washed away even by blood. The inexpiable and grave guilt of discord is not cleansed even by suffering. He cannot be a martyr who is not in the Church. He will not be able to reach the kingdom who has abandoned her who is going to reign. Christ gave us peace; he commanded us to be in harmony and of one mind; he charged us to keep the covenants of affection and love uncorrupted and inviolate. He cannot show himself a martyr who has not held to brotherly love. The apostle Paul teaches and bears witness to this when he says: “If I have faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing. And if I distribute all my goods as food, and if I hand over my body so that I may burn, but do not have love, I gain nothing” (1 Corinthians 13:2-3). “Love is patient, love is kind, love is not jealous, is not puffed up, is not provoked, does not act wrongly, does not think evil, loves all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love will never fall away” (1 Corinthians 13:4-8). “Never,” he says, “will love fall away.” For this will always be in the kingdom; this will endure forever in the unity of a brotherhood that holds together. Discord cannot reach the kingdom of heaven. No one who has violated Christ’s love by faithless dissension will be able to attain the reward of Christ, who said: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you” (John 15:12). He who does not have love does not have God. This is the voice of the blessed apostle John: “God,” he says, “is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him” (1 John 4:16). They cannot remain with God who have refused to be of one mind in the Church of God. Though they may burn, handed over to flames and fires, or throw their lives to beasts, that will not be the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness, nor the glorious outcome of religious virtue but the ruin of despair. Such a person can be killed, but cannot be crowned. He professes himself a Christian in the same way that the devil often pretends to be Christ, as the Lord himself warns and says: “Many will come in my name, saying: I am Christ, and they will deceive many” (Mark 13:6). Just as that one is not Christ, though he deceives in the name, so neither can he be seen as a Christian who does not remain in Christ’s gospel and in the truth of the faith.

last_rejected.source_quote: et si habuero fidem ita ut montes transferam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil sum: et si in cibos distribuero omnia mea et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil proficio
last_rejected.why: The quotation combines 1 Cor 13:2 and 13:3 but cites only 13:2-3; the 'ut ardeam' clause matches 13:3, but the citation should cover 13:2-3 or be split.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation 13:2-3 correctly covers both quoted verses; claim contradicts itself, calling it both wrong and correct.

last_rejected.source_quote: caritas magnanima est, caritas benigna est, caritas non aemulatur, non inflatur, non inritatur, non agit perperam, non cogitat malum, omnia diligit, omnia credit, omnia sperat, omnia sustinet. caritas numquam excidet
last_rejected.why: The quotation ends at 'caritas numquam excidet' which is 13:8a, but citation says 13:4-8 which includes more material not quoted.
last_rejected.ruling: 13:4-8a is standard citation for this excerpt; omitting 13:8b's final clause doesn't break the reference.
